newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, hoteliers firmer.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, hoteliers firmer.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday, with slight correction among blue chips and gains for hoteliers, while traders predicted prices would continue to grow but at a slower pace.
"I definitely see a trend of moderate growth in the coming days and weeks," said Nenad Pavletic, a trader with Auctor brokerage.
"The interest of international investors will keep boosting the prices and, more importantly, help stabilise them on higher levels," he said.
Pavletic singled out Zagrebacka Banka E-series preference issue, traded at about half of the price of the more popular A-series shares, as the potential "best buy".

"These are very good shares and I am glad that they have been 'discovered': on top of the 7-percent guaranteed dividend, the holder has a voting right. They are as good as ordinary shares, if not better, and they are twice as cheap," Pavletic said.
Both Zagrebacka issues edged down on Thursday -- A-series 10 kuna to 1,900 and E-series 15 kuna to 985 -- on relatively modest volume of 456 and 400 shares, respectively.

Another blue chip, drug firm Pliva, lost eight kuna to close at 502, following developments in London where its Global Depository Recepits (GDRs), issued at 10 per share, were traded in a $16.5-$16.7 range, down from $17.435 last week.
Pavletic said the correction of both leading shares was expected and even welcomed after their steep rise in 1997.
Among the losers was also food processor Podravka, which lost 38 kuna to 330 on Thursday's record volume of 5,033 shares.
Top gainer was Istrian hotelier Laguna from Porec, which added 80 kuna to 1,495 -- close to its all time high of 1,560 recorded last October.
Other hoteliers pushed up as well, albeit not so dramatically. Istraturist rose 20 kuna to 220 and Jadranturist five to 335 on high volume of 2,073 and 1,512 shares, respectively.
"A good sign is not so much the price, but the fact that hotel stocks are becoming liquid again," Pavletic said.
Of 11 active issues, six were down, four up while one remained flat. Volume was slightly lower at 11,489 shares, turnover unchanged at 4.9 million kuna.
